title: The functionality of the addressbook is frustrating
creator: moby.duck
content:
The functionality of the addressbook is very frustrating to me.

I have about 1000 contacts in my addressbook, which I'd love to sort into groups. And when writing an email to a certain group, I would like to display the list of that group in the sidebar of the Email. However, this is only possible when I make a new addressbook for each group, because only addressbooks are displayed as a list with all the contacts contained.

Now most of my contacts are in several different groups/addressbooks (for example, "Steve" is in my "hiking" group and also in my "work" and "neighborhood" group). However, one contact can only be in one addressbook. Meaning if I want to add Steve to the different groups/addressbooks, I have to copy his contacts three times to be able to put him in the three different groups/addressbooks. Doing this for all the contacts I have, it would get cluttered very much, very soon. Which I find super frustrating because it can get very confusing and it just seems so unneccessary. The other frustrating thing about this is, you can't just copy a contact, but you have to create a contact manually each time or via the "save email" button in received emails. But the latter can also be confusing because the format of the saved contact can vary; Steve can either be "Steve Smith" one time, but also "NameIThoughtWasCoolWhenIwas12@narf.org" another time.

What I'd love to have is ONE profile for each contact where I can put in all the information I have/need/want and that profile can be part of several different groups. If a contact has more than one email in their profile (i.e. privat, work), I'd ideally be able to attach one email to one group and another email to a different group. And obviously, the group can also be displayed as a list in the sidebar while writing an email (just like addressbooks are now).

I don't know how it can be implemented (keywords, tags?), but it would be great if it was possible.

I also don't know if it is possible already and I'm just to slow to get it. So if anyone knows a) how to add a contact to several addressbooks without having to copy the contact each time or b) how to display a mailing list as a list in the sidebar, I'm all ears.

title: Outlook.com SMTP error 535 – OAuth2 authentication fails in Thunderbird
creator: sergio.sgambati
content:
Hello Thunderbird Support Team,

I am experiencing a persistent SMTP authentication failure when sending emails from my personal Outlook.com account using Thunderbird.

My configuration:

Operating system: Windows 11 Pro (64-bit)

Thunderbird version: 159.0 (32-bit)

Account type: Personal Outlook.com account

What works:

Receiving emails via IMAP works correctly.

Sending and receiving emails through Outlook.com webmail works correctly.

My other Microsoft email account works in Thunderbird.

What does not work:

Sending emails from my new Outlook.com account through Thunderbird consistently fails.

The SMTP server returns:

535 Authentication unsuccessful – SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox.

Outgoing SMTP settings

Server: smtp-mail.outlook.com

Port: 587

Connection security: STARTTLS

Authentication method: OAuth2

Username: Full Outlook.com email address

Troubleshooting already performed

Checked all SMTP server settings.

Verified that OAuth2 is selected.

Removed previously saved authentication credentials.

Repeated Microsoft OAuth2 authentication successfully.

Retested sending messages. The same error persists.

Thunderbird's Error Console confirms that the failure occurs during the AUTH XOAUTH2 authentication exchange.

The server explicitly reports that SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox.

Questions

Is this a known Thunderbird issue affecting SMTP OAuth2 authentication with personal Outlook.com accounts?

Could Thunderbird be generating an incorrect XOAUTH2 authentication request?

Can Thunderbird provide a more detailed SMTP diagnostic log to identify the cause?

Does this error indicate that Microsoft's SMTP service is rejecting an otherwise valid OAuth2 authentication request?

Is there any known workaround or can this issue be escalated to the Thunderbird developers?

I would appreciate a technical investigation rather than another general configuration guide, as the standard troubleshooting steps have already been completed.

Thank you for your help.
